People are told to eat the lawful and good and not follow Satan, a clear enemy who orders evil, immorality and saying about Allah what they do not know.
Believers are told to eat good things Allah provided and thank Him; only dead animals, blood, swine and what is dedicated to other than Allah are forbidden, except under necessity.
All food was lawful to the Children of Israel except what Israel forbade himself before the Torah; whoever invents lies about Allah after that is a wrongdoer.
Believers must fulfill contracts; grazing livestock is lawful to them except what is recited, but hunting is not permitted while in ihram.
Dead animals, blood and pork are forbidden and the religion is perfected; good foods, the food of those given the Scripture and marriage to their chaste women are lawful.
Believers must not forbid the good things Allah made lawful, nor transgress, but eat what He provided that is lawful and good, and fear Him.
Eat what Allah's name has been mentioned over and not what it has not; what is forbidden is detailed except under compulsion, and leave sin, apparent and concealed.
Eat of the crops and livestock without excess; their bans are questioned, and the Prophet's revelation forbids only carrion, spilled blood, swine and what is dedicated to other than Allah.

Take adornment at every masjid, eat and drink without excess; Allah's adornment and good provision are not forbidden, only immoralities, sin, oppression, associating partners and speaking of Him without knowledge.
People are asked whether Allah permitted them to make some of His provision lawful and some unlawful, or whether they invent lies about Him.
Eat what Allah provides, lawful and good; He forbids only dead animals, blood, swine and what is dedicated to others, and no one may falsely declare things lawful or unlawful.
